items.title: Ramsar Sites in India
items.summary: 25 OCT 2026 9:43AM by PIB Delhi India’s network of Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention has expanded nearly fourfold since 2014. It has grown from 26 to 103 designated sites covering over 13.87 lakh hectares. Ranking first in Asia and third globally, these ecosystems safeguard biodiversity, buffer floods, recharge groundwater, and sustain livelihoods.

facts.text: 25 OCT 2026 9:43AM by PIB Delhi India’s network of Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention has expanded nearly fourfold since 2014.
It has grown from 26 to 103 designated sites covering over 13.87 lakh hectares.
It was adopted at Ramsar, Iran, on 2 February 1971 and entered into force in 1975.
As on October 2026, it now includes 172 Contracting Parties and over 2,536 designated " Ramsar Sites " worldwide.
